bull.b: Repeated year-over-year growth indicates expanding adoption of SKYX products rather than a single-period sales spike. Sustained top-line momentum can improve operating leverage, support broader commercial deployments, and strengthen the company’s position as smart-building adoption develops.

Deako broadens SKYX’s product coverage from ceiling infrastructure to wall-based smart controls and adds builder access. If integration succeeds, the combined platform may increase cross-selling, expand deployment opportunities, and create a more comprehensive smart-building offering.

A larger cash balance, lower operating burn, and debt reduction improve near-term financial flexibility while the company scales deployments. Although cash generation is not yet positive, this direction of change gives management more capacity to fund operations and pursue its 2026 targets.

bear.b: Deep and persistent operating losses show that current revenue scale has not yet translated into a self-sustaining earnings model. Continued losses can limit reinvestment, increase reliance on external capital, and make profitability dependent on substantial execution and operating leverage.

The business continues to consume cash rather than fund itself through operations, leaving management dependent on its cash balance or financing. This constrains flexibility during deployment growth and makes the target of becoming cash-flow positive by the end of 2026 important but unproven.

Meaningful leverage already limits financial flexibility, while the Deako transaction adds a costly secured obligation with near- and medium-term maturities. Higher interest and repayment demands could absorb cash needed for growth and increase pressure if integration or deployment benefits arrive slowly.
